title: Ampere SM80 Architecture for CuTe DSL
critical_patterns: Use cp.async for non-blocking GMEM to SMEM transfers
Pipeline with 3+ stages for latency hiding
Prefer FP16/BF16 for compute, FP32 for accumulation
Use TF32 for FP32 range with faster performance
constraints: A matrix must be 2:4 sparse for sparse MMA
Shared memory configuration affects register availability and occupancy
TF32 is automatically used for FP32 GEMM operations on Tensor Cores
compressed_summary: The Ampere SM80 architecture introduces significant advancements for deep learning workloads, primarily through enhanced Tensor Cores, asynchronous memory operations, and structural sparsity. Key features include support for various data types like FP16, BF16, TF32, and INT8, with Tensor Cores providing substantial performance improvements. Asynchronous copy operations (cp.async) enable overlapping data movement with computation, crucial for maximizing throughput. Structural sparsity (2:4 sparsity) offers a 2x speedup by ensuring only two non-zero values in every four-value group. Multi-stage pipelining, especially with 3+ stages, is recommended to fully utilize Tensor Cores and hide memory latency. Shared memory configuration is flexible, with up to 164 KB available per SM, but requires careful tuning to balance register usage and occupancy. TF32 provides a middle ground between FP16 and FP32, offering faster computation with a slightly reduced precision. Best practices include leveraging async copy for all global to shared memory transfers, using multi-stage pipelines, preferring mixed precision with FP16/BF16 for compute, and optimizing shared memory sizes for specific workloads. Performance tuning involves selecting appropriate tile sizes and stage counts, with typical GEMM implementations achieving 80-90% of the theoretical peak performance on the A100 GPU.
